You now have a way of seeing your own sport studies that will serve you in every module from here on. Each assessment you meet is a chance to show what you have learned, each piece of feedback a pointer to what to do next, and the two together are how your work improves across the degree, right up to your independent project. The habit to keep is simple: read what each task is asking, use the feedback you get, and let it shape the next report or plan.

That same habit carries into professional sport. Wherever you are given work, judged against a standard, and told how to improve, as a coach, a scientist, a manager or a therapist, the people who get better are the ones who treat each round as feeding the next. The cycle you have just learned to see is one you will use long after you graduate.
